    - Sit on the fiddler's other knee if you like, Ferro won't mind. Don't ask for anything slow. I don't do slow.

    - I come from a very respectable family of court musicians in Selsior. Fiddle at four. Slow dances, nothing but slow dances. So I sped them up a little. Then a lot. Then at a guild dinner the dancers gave up and ran.
    - I left at seventeen. They still write once a year, very politely. When the letter comes I play the slowest dance they ever taught me as fast as I possibly can. It's how we talk.
    - Drum! Drum has a rhythm for every one of my nine and never says a word about them. And there's a thin person with a tin whistle who hangs about the edge of the square every time I play. Never plays it. Just holds it. Strange.
    - Drum, always. And Piper, now, with the tin whistle. A second part for every one of my nine, written out, and never asked. Can you imagine? Nine. I'm writing the tenth with the whistle in it from the start.
    - Go! I've got a tune to finish and you're slowing it down. Nicely. But still.
